newsitem.title: UK: UK PENSIONS SECOND LOWEST IN EU - STUDY.
newsitem.headline: UK PENSIONS SECOND LOWEST IN EU - STUDY.

text.p: Average British retirees can expect pension benefits equal to 77 percent of net earnings, the second lowest benefit level in the European Union, according to a study released Thursday.
Consultants Sedgwick Noble Lowndes found that only Finnish retirees -- at 73 percent of net earnings -- fare worse.
Greeks come out with the highest level, at 103 percent. They are closely followed by the Germans and the Italians, whose pensions replace 94 and 95 percent of earnings, respectively.
British higher earners are slightly better positioned, according to the study, with employees making four times the national average receiving pensions equal to 80 percent of net earnings.
"In Britain we have a highly developed private pension system that allows people to build up pensions to supplement their state benefits," said David King, a director at Sedgwick Noble Lowndes.
"The system is best geared to people who can afford to make contributions from their salary."
"Clearly there are shortcomings in the UK system, especially for those people who cannot take advantage of private occupational pension plans," King said.
"The government's proposals for a new supplementary scheme should go some way towards bridging the gap."
Average French employees also get 77 percent in pensions, while retirees in the Netherlands get 82 percent.
The figures reflect pensions from both mandatory and voluntary schemes after deductions for income tax and benefit contributions.
